features.title: User registration and login

Check Firebase Auth console — user appears

features.title: User home location setup
features.user_visible_behavior: On first login, user is prompted to set home location (auto-filled from GPS, editable on map). `homeGeohash` is written to the Firestore user document. Without this, FCM alerts cannot be targeted.
verification: First login → home location prompt appears
Tap 'Use my location' → GPS coordinate auto-fills
Confirm → Firestore user document has `homeLat`, `homeLng`, `homeGeohash` set
Navigate to Profile and edit home location → Firestore updates
features.evidence: useAuth.ts: onSnapshot listener on users doc; exposes needsHomeSetup=!homeGeohash. _layout.tsx: redirects to /home-setup when needsHomeSetup is true (waits for profile load before redirecting). home-setup.tsx: Location.getCurrentPositionAsync + geohashForLocation precision 7 + updateDoc. profile.tsx: shows coords and Edit button navigating to /home-setup?edit=1. TypeScript: 0 errors. Requires live device test to move to passing.
features.notes: Critical path for push notifications. homeGeohash must be set or users never receive alerts.

features.title: Flood report submission

verification: Tap Report button → ReportSheet slides up
GPS location auto-fills (latitude + longitude shown)
Select each depth option (ankle/knee/waist/chest) — color changes correctly per DEPTH_CONFIG
Tap Submit → ConfirmToast appears
Check Firestore `reports` collection — document created with correct fields: lat, lng, geohash, depth, userId, status='pending', trustScore=60, corroborationCount=1, expiresAt=reportedAt+6h
Confirm `onReportCreate` Cloud Function ran (check Firebase Function logs)
features.evidence: ReportSheet.tsx: addDoc with lat/lng/geohash(precision 7)/depth/reportedAt/expiresAt(+6h)/userId/accountAgeDays(computed from metadata.creationTime)/upvotes=0/downvotes=0/status=pending/corroborationCount=1/trustScore=60. features.title: Live map with real-time flood pins
features.user_visible_behavior: Map screen shows colored pins for all active (non-expired) reports. Pins update in real time via Firestore listener. Pin color matches DEPTH_CONFIG. Tapping a pin shows depth, time, and upvote/downvote buttons.
verification: Open map screen — no errors in console
Submit a test report from a second device/account → pin appears on map without refresh
Verify pin color: ankle=amber, knee=coral, waist=red, chest=darkred
Expire a report manually (set expiresAt to now) → pin disappears within one listener cycle
Tap a pin → detail sheet shows depth label, time since report
features.evidence: useReports.ts: onSnapshot with status in ['pending','confirmed'] + client-side expiresAt>now() guard (static Timestamp.now() in query is insufficient for mid-session expiry). FloodPin.tsx: single-tap onPress on Marker opens detail sheet directly; tracksViewChanges=false for performance; Callout removed. alert.tsx: added timeAgo() helper + Reported MetaRow showing time since reportedAt. TypeScript: 0 errors. Requires live device test to move to passing.
features.notes: useReports hook must filter by status in ['pending','confirmed'] and expiresAt > now().

features.title: Flood-aware route overlay (Option A)
features.user_visible_behavior: User types a destination in the search bar that floats above the map. A blue polyline route is drawn on the map. Each flood report within 200m of the route is ringed with a colored warning circle. A banner shows '3 flood zones on your route · 18 mins (5.2 km)' or 'Route looks clear · 12 mins (3.1 km)'. Tapping × clears the route.
verification: Type a destination and press Search → blue route polyline appears on map
Flood report within 200m of route → colored warning circle appears + banner shows flood count
Flood report > 200m from route → no warning circle, banner shows 'Route looks clear'
Tap × → route and circles clear from map
Missing EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_DIRECTIONS_API_KEY → error banner shown
TypeScript: 0 errors in mobile/
features.notes: Requires EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_DIRECTIONS_API_KEY in mobile/.env (Google Maps Directions API). No new npm packages — polyline decoding is implemented inline in mobile/lib/routeUtils.ts. Flood proximity threshold: 200m from any route segment.

features.title: Corroboration counter and confirmed status
features.user_visible_behavior: When 3 independent reports arrive within 500m and 30 minutes of each other, the earliest report's status changes to 'confirmed' and its pin changes appearance (e.g. solid fill vs outline). `corroborationCount` on each report reflects self-inclusive count.
verification: Submit 3 reports from 3 different user accounts within 500m (use simulated coordinates if needed)
Check Firestore — third report triggers status='confirmed' on the cluster
Verify corroborationCount = nearby.length + 1 on each report doc
Confirm confirmed pin has distinct visual state on map
features.evidence: onReportCreate.ts: getNearbyReports([lat,lng], 0.5, 30, reportId) → corroborationCount=nearby.length+1 → isConfirmed=count>=3 → batch writes status='confirmed' + corroborationCount to current report and FieldValue.increment(1)+status='confirmed' (if not already) to each neighbor. geo.ts: getNearbyReports uses geohash bounds query (GeoFire standard pattern) with status in ['pending','confirmed'] server-side, then client-side filters expiresAt>now + reportedAt within 30min + haversine<=0.5km. FloodPin.tsx: isConfirmed=status==='confirmed' → full opacity; pending → opacity:0.65. alert.tsx: shows corroborationCount as 'N nearby'. TypeScript: 0 errors in functions/ and mobile/. Requires live Firebase deploy + 3-report test to move to passing.
features.notes: corroborationCount is self-inclusive (own report + nearby). Threshold is >= 3. expiresAt filter is applied client-side (not server-side) to avoid a Firestore multi-inequality-field restriction with the geohash range query.

features.title: Severity fast-path preliminary alert
features.user_visible_behavior: A single waist or chest depth report with trustScore >= 65 immediately triggers a push notification to nearby users, labelled 'Unverified report nearby'. This fires without waiting for 3 corroborations.
verification: Submit a 'chest' depth report from a fresh account on-road in rainy conditions (trustScore = 70 base, no penalties → 70 >= 65 ✓)
Second device within 2km receives Expo push notification within ~10 seconds
Notification title is 'Unverified flood report nearby'
Check Cloud Function logs — sendNearbyNotifications called with preliminary=true
Tap notification on second device → app opens to /alert?reportId=... screen
features.evidence: onReportCreate.ts: base trustScore raised to 70 so on-road+rainy reports (no penalties) reach 70 >= 65 threshold. notifyNearby.ts: replaced Firebase Admin SDK messaging.sendEachForMulticast with Expo Push API (POST https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/send) — correct for Expo managed workflow with Expo push tokens. Stale token cleanup uses Expo DeviceNotRegistered error code. useNotifications.ts: getExpoPushTokenAsync now passes projectId from Constants.expoConfig?.extra?.eas?.projectId (required in SDK 56); fails gracefully with console.warn if not configured. _layout.tsx: Notifications.useLastNotificationResponse() navigates to /alert?reportId=... when user taps a notification. app.json: expo-notifications plugin added. admin.ts: removed unused messaging export. TypeScript: 0 errors in functions/ and mobile/. Requires EAS projectId in eas.json + live device + Cloud Function deploy to move to passing.
features.notes: trustScore base is now 70. On-road + rainy (no penalties) = 70 >= 65 → fast-path fires. On-road + dry = 55 → no fast-path (intended). Expo Push API used instead of Firebase Admin SDK — requires EAS projectId configured in eas.json for Expo token registration to succeed.

features.title: FCM push notifications on confirmed reports
features.user_visible_behavior: When a report reaches confirmed status, all users with homeGeohash within 2km receive an FCM push notification. Tapping the notification opens the map centered on the report.
verification: Set homeGeohash on test user within 2km of test report location
Trigger confirmation (3 corroborating reports)
FCM notification arrives on test device within ~5 seconds
Notification payload contains: street, depth, reportedAt, reportId
Tap notification → app opens and map centers on the confirmed report
Test user outside 2km does NOT receive notification
features.evidence: onReportCreate.ts: reverseGeocode() runs in parallel with snapToRoad/rainfall/lastReport using Nominatim free API (no key, User-Agent header, fail open → undefined). street + reportedAt passed to sendNearbyNotifications. notifyNearby.ts: body uses street when available ('Knee-deep flooding on Nguyen Hue' vs fallback 'in your area'); data payload includes {reportId, depth, reportedAt, street, lat, lng, preliminary}. FloodMap.tsx: MapView ref + animateToRegion(lat,lng,delta=0.01) when centerOn prop changes. index.tsx: reads focusLat/focusLng from useLocalSearchParams, passes as centerOn to FloodMap. _layout.tsx: notification tap extracts lat/lng from data, navigates to /(tabs)/ with focusLat/focusLng params then pushes /alert. TypeScript: 0 errors. Requires EAS projectId + live 3-report test + 2-device test to move to passing.
features.notes: Expo Push API (not Firebase Admin SDK messaging). Street name via Nominatim reverse geocoding — fails open (notification still sent without street). getUsersNearby uses homeGeohash geohash bounds + haversine filter at exactly 2km.

features.title: Report auto-expiry (6 hours)
features.user_visible_behavior: Reports older than 6 hours automatically disappear from the live map. The scheduled Cloud Function runs every 30 minutes and sets status='expired' on overdue reports.
verification: Deploy `expireReports` scheduled function (every 30 minutes)
Manually set a report's expiresAt to 1 minute ago in Firestore
Wait for next scheduled run (or manually trigger via Firebase console)
Confirm report status = 'expired' in Firestore
Confirm pin disappears from live map
features.evidence: expireReports.ts: onSchedule 'every 30 minutes' asia-southeast1. Query scoped to status in ['pending','confirmed','disputed'] + expiresAt < now — uses existing composite index {status ASCENDING, expiresAt ASCENDING} so it never scans historical expired docs. Batch writes chunked at 500-doc BATCH_LIMIT to respect Firestore batch cap. useReports.ts: onSnapshot with status in ['pending','confirmed'] + client-side expiresAt>now guard; when expireReports updates status→'expired', the doc drops out of the live query automatically, removing the pin. TypeScript: 0 errors. expireReports exported from index.ts. Requires firebase deploy --only functions to verify.
features.notes: For demo: manually trigger in Firebase console (Functions → expireReports → Actions → Trigger) rather than waiting 30 min. Pin disappears because useReports status filter already excludes 'expired'.

features.title: Still flooded / Looks clear upvote and downvote
features.user_visible_behavior: Tapping a map pin shows upvote ('Still flooded') and downvote ('Looks clear') buttons. Tapping increments the corresponding counter on the Firestore document. Counts update in real time.
verification: Tap a pin → detail sheet shows current upvote and downvote counts
Tap 'Still flooded' → Firestore upvotes field increments by 1
Tap 'Looks clear' → Firestore downvotes field increments by 1
Second device sees updated counts without refresh
Firestore security rules only allow upvotes/downvotes to be updated (not other fields)
features.evidence: alert.tsx: switched from getDoc (one-shot) to onSnapshot (live listener) so vote counts update in real time on all devices viewing the same report; unsub returned from useEffect for cleanup. vote() uses updateDoc + increment(1) (atomic, no race condition). Optimistic local setReport runs immediately; onSnapshot confirms with server value moments later. firestore.rules: non-owner update restricted to affectedKeys().hasOnly(['upvotes','downvotes']) — already correct from session 2. TypeScript: 0 errors. Requires live device test to move to passing.
features.notes: onSnapshot on the alert doc also picks up status changes (e.g. confirmed → disputed) in real time, which is a free bonus. No per-user vote deduplication — acceptable for demo scope.

features.title: Disputed status trigger
features.user_visible_behavior: When a report accumulates downvotes > upvotes + 5 AND downvotes >= 3, an onUpdate Cloud Function sets its status to 'disputed'. Disputed reports show a different visual state on the map.
verification: Set upvotes=10, downvotes=20 → status='disputed' (20 > 10+5 and 20>=3) ✓
Set upvotes=10, downvotes=14 → status stays unchanged (14 is not > 10+5=15) ✓
Votes swing back (downvotes drop or upvotes rise) → status restores to confirmed/pending ✓
Map shows disputed pins as grey fill + orange border ✓
Note: verification step 'upvotes=0, downvotes=3 → disputed' in original spec is incorrect — 3 is not > 0+5=5, so it correctly stays pending
features.evidence: notifyNearby.ts onReportUpdate: dispute trigger (downvotes>=3 && downvotes>upvotes+5) unchanged. Fixed two bugs: (1) infinite loop — clearing branch now guards with after.status==='disputed' so setting status='pending' does not retrigger itself; (2) restores to 'confirmed' if corroborationCount>=3, else 'pending' — was always writing 'pending'. useReports.ts: added 'disputed' to status filter so disputed pins appear on map. FloodPin.tsx: status==='disputed' renders grey fill (#9E9E9E) + orange border (#FF9800); pending keeps 65% opacity; confirmed keeps full depth color. TypeScript: 0 errors. Requires live deploy + Firestore console test to move to passing.
features.notes: Original verification step 1 (upvotes=0, downvotes=3 → disputed) is wrong: 3 is not > 0+5=5. Use upvotes=0, downvotes=6 for a correct threshold test. The onUpdate trigger fires on every vote write, so disputed status transitions within 1-2 seconds of the triggering vote.
